title: Resource governance (CPU cap)
summary: Sustained, well-planned reporting at more concurrency than the target has vCores: a full utilization rollup with a per-row scoring hash, parallelism allowed. On Azure SQL Database it drives CPU to the service objective's limit, so the database is throttled rather than slowed by a bad plan; on SQL Server it's plain CPU saturation. The fix is capacity or scheduling, not a rewrite, which contrasts with cpu-pressure.

concurrency.description: Reporting sessions; more than the vCore limit to reach the cap.

intensity.description: Hashing work per row (1 to 4 passes) and a shorter pause between reports.

notes.T3: Consumes serverless vCore seconds (and the free offer's monthly allowance) while it runs; the default is 5 minutes.
notes.T1: Shows as CPU saturation of the VM, not a service-objective cap.

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerCPUUtilization at the tier limit on T3 (or near 100% of the VM on T1 and T2)
SqlServerWaitStats: CPU wait category (SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD) with healthy plans
SqlServerActiveSessions: ContosoCare.Demo/resource-governance sessions running in parallel
A capacity or CPU-limit finding for the database
expectedHubSignals.note: Preview; coverage by target is undocumented (ADR 0013).

expectedSymptoms: CPU pinned at the limit while every plan is sound
Report duration grows with concurrency because the sessions share a capped CPU
On T3, sys.dm_db_resource_stats shows avg_cpu_percent near 100
queryLevelEvidence: sys.dm_db_resource_stats (Azure SQL Database) or sys.dm_os_ring_buffers scheduler monitor (SQL Server)
Query Store: one report query with high total CPU and a stable, reasonable plan
reset: Read-only; nothing to undo. Stopping the run returns CPU to the baseline; T3 auto-pauses after its delay once no session is open.
